newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal halts three private radio broadcasters.
newsitem.headline: Senegal halts three private radio broadcasters.

text.p: The Senegalese government on Saturday stopped three private radio stations from operating for three months for not paying their broadcasting fees, the station managers said.
The decision to stop SUD FM, Nostalgie and Dunya from broadcasting was notified to the stations' management on Friday evening by Senegal's Minister of Communications, Serigne Diop.
International broadcasters such as Radio France International, Africa Numero 1 and the BBC can still be heard on the FM band in Senegal.
Sud FM owes the state 20 million CFA francs ($32,000), while Dunya FM and Nostalgie owe 30 million.

According to the management of SUD FM, only three other countries in West Africa demand broadcasting fees. In Mali and Gambia it is a symbolic amount, while Ivory Coast takes a percentage of a station's turnover.
